reviews.comment: Dr. Seipp is so passionate about history. He always made me want to go to class to learn more, but make sure you go to class. He lectures from the start of class to the end of class using the full amount of time. If you miss one lecture, you better catch up because you probably missed vital info. Overall great professor and I HIGHLY recommend him!
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Seipp is one of the most inspiring and passionate professors I have ever had. You WILL have to WORK and READ for a good grade, but he is there to help. Attendance isn't mandatory, but exams come straight from lecture. This is the only class I've ever had where the class applauded the teacher and shook his hand the last day. Take him.

Phenomenal lecturer and storyteller. 2 short answer exams that, w/ adequate lecture notes, were easy to prepare for. 4 merciful book quizzes that he only administered to ensure that everyone made an effort to be familiar with topics involved in class discussions. 1 group project that was actually interesting to research. Take his class if you can!

You need to go to the lectures but you'll want to go. His lectures are amazing and it's almost likely he's telling a story. He gives you key terms that are important and as long as you have great notes on those then the rest of your notes can be less detailed. Easily my favorite professor I had at Texas A&M.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Seipp was incredible! If I could take him for all my history courses I would. He is very passionate about what he teaches. There were about five books we had to read, and a quiz for each book. The quizzes are super easy if you read.

He great and really passionate about his classes. Class is mandatory because he doesn't use a textbook or have lecture slides online, so the notes are what he says in class. Always gives you a heads up about no classes or change of office hours.

Adam Seipp is on his way to becoming the premier military/german history professor at A&M. Always ready to receive questions, very available to help outside of class, passionate about what he teaches, presents history in ways that it is real and important to us; in essence, he brings humanity to history, with a dash of humor, and powerful emotions.
